https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yKlJeqkeUgY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解全球超過七成網站採用的 PHP 核心重大漏洞危機，以及這場被資安界稱為「黑色十月」事件的波及規模。
  • 揭秘人工智慧（AI）在資安攻防戰中的雙重角色，探討 AI 如何突破過去人力的限制，讓原本極難觸發的漏洞演變為真實威脅。
  • 掌握網站管理者與一般網路使用者在面對大規模零日攻擊時，應採取的具體自保建議與安全防護措施。

摘要

全球七成網站面臨的「黑色十月」危機

作者指出，全球超過 70% 網站使用的後端程式語言 PHP 爆出嚴重的核心安全漏洞。若未即時修補，駭客將能直接繞過網站介面並接管伺服器，使大量商業機密、個資暴露於危險之中。為了防堵損害擴大，美國國家安全局與荷蘭國家網路安全中心均建議停用相關對外網站，導致全球眾多政府機關、醫院、銀行及維基百科部分系統緊急離線；日本軟銀亦因緊急修補該漏洞，一度造成災害警報系統無法正常發布。

AI 介入挖掘：沉睡二十年的複雜漏洞重見天日

作者解釋，PHP 就如同網站幕後負責處理登入、搜尋與運算的工作人員，已存在超過三十年。過去該漏洞雖曾被發現，但因攻擊路徑極其複雜，資安界普遍認為難以利用。然而，加州資安公司與科技巨頭藉由 OpenAI 的先進語言模型，成功在極短時間內找到繞過限制並接管網站的方法。作者表示，這顯示在 AI 輔助下，過往需要龐大團隊在數百萬行程式碼中耗費數年才能尋得的微小瑕疵，如今單一人員即可迅速發掘並發動高複雜度的攻擊。

補丁外洩的搶修賽跑與 AI 帶來的資安兩難

在發現漏洞後，工程團隊日夜兼程修改了近百億個檔案與上萬行程式碼，原訂於 10 月 22 日釋出修補更新。不料情報提前兩天遭外洩，迫使官方將修復檔案提前至 10 月 21 日釋出以防範未然。作者強調，發布補丁並不代表危機結束，因為駭客也能透過逆向工程研究漏洞或尋找新破綻。雖然在補丁公開前後出現數以百萬計的攻擊嘗試，但所幸目前尚無成功的重大入侵案例，然而專家對 AI 是否讓攻擊端占據上風的疑慮依舊分歧。

大眾應對指引與數位防護之道

針對這場風暴，作者釐清指出，除非使用者自行架設並管理網站，否則一般網友無須為此下載特定補丁或更新手機電腦。作者提醒，自行架站者應立即更新至最新版本的 PHP；而一般大眾為了長遠的數位安全，應落實不重複使用同一組密碼的原則，並為手機、電腦與智慧聯網家電開啟自動軟體更新，以降低在其他連鎖攻擊中受害的風險。

================================================

Before we start today's main news, we have an announcement: with only one month left until the November 28th local elections, have you decided who you're voting for? Next Tuesday at 8 PM , I’ll be inviting "Human Scum Text" columnist Chou to host a livestream in our LINE community, "Fan-Chieh's International News Discussion Forum." We’ll be discussing some of the more intense mayoral races—for instance, can Shen Pu-yang and Su Chiao-hui really flip the Taipei and New Taipei results? If you haven't joined the forum yet, scan this QR code now to. join; you can also see what international news everyone is following on a regular basis. If you have any questions for the current candidates, feel free to leave them for us in the discussion thread. Next up is today's main news. Last Thursday, while everyone was busy wondering if they’d get a typhoon day off, software engineers around the world were working themselves to death, unable to sleep because a major security vulnerability was discovered in PHP, the programming language used by over 70%of websites globally. If not patched immediately,. your site could be hijacked by hackers at any time, meaning 70%of the world's websites were at risk. This is a huge deal, and many sites went offline urgently for repairs. So, there was actually a wave of websites going offline last Thursday. I know everyone was only focused on the typhoon day at the time, so you might not have noticed that many sites were inaccessible. A weekend has passed; has the problem been solved? In four words: "Proceed with caution," it’s too early to let your guard down. The most interesting.

part of this whole affair is that the vulnerability was discovered by AI; if it weren't for AI, humanity might have ...Hello everyone, I’m Fan-Chieh, and welcome to Fan-Chieh’s Take. Let’s first look at the extent of the damage. The US National Security Agency and the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre recommended that any public-facing website should be taken offline until the issue is fixed. As a result, a massive number of government, hospital, school, and bank websites were. temporarily taken down, and even Wikipedia, which everyone uses, had to temporarily disable some of its systems . In Japan, besides Prime Minister Kishida posting on X to urge businesses to pay attention to the PHP issue, Japan’s disaster warning system was temporarily unable to issue alerts because SoftBank was urgently patching the PHP vulnerability. At this point, you must be wondering: what exactly is this PHP? Why is it such a serious issue? PHP stands for Hypertext Preprocessor, and it is a programming. language that allows websites to function. You can think of a website as a restaurant; when we enter a URL to open a page, it’s just like walking into a restaurant to order a meal. At this point, the computer behind the website, the server, follows the instructions written in PHP to process our request and sends the results back to our phone or computer so we can see the content on the webpage. Things like logging into an account, searching for products, or checking items in a shopping cart all likely require PHP to help process them. In simple terms, PHP.

is like the staff working behind the scenes of a website; although we can't see it, it gets things done. PHP has been used for over 30 years and is the foundation of the foundation for how websites operate. The reason this issue is so serious is that this vulnerability exists within PHP's core system. To give you an analogy, many people use the Windows operating system on their computers. If a bug appears in the core of Windows, then every computer running that Windows operating system will have that bug. This PHP. vulnerability is the same; since the problem is in the PHP core, if any website using PHP doesn't update its code as soon as possible, hackers who know about this vulnerability can attack these websites and steal all their data. That’s why sites like government websites or large corporate sites holding vast amounts of customer data or trade secrets could become prime targets for hackers. This is why various countries urgently took their public sector websites offline, waiting until the PHP issue was fixed before bringing them back up. There is another. key reason why this problem is so severe: this vulnerability allows hackers to bypass the website interface , directly control the computer running the site, and gain access to all data. It’s like hiding your house key under a potted plant by the door; once a thief knows where the key is, they can walk right through the front door and steal your things. That’s ridiculous, has no one discovered this problem in the last 20 years? They had, but back then, everyone thought this vulnerability was too complex. Even for brilliant hackers, it was very.

difficult to launch an attack this way, so the hole was just left there. Unexpectedly, OpenAI's AI not only discovered this hole but also found a way to easily bypass it. Discover. This goes back to August of this year, when researchers at a California cybersecurity firm used OpenAI's most advanced language model to look for PHP vulnerabilities. They ended up finding this flaw and a way to exploit it,. taking over small websites in just seconds, and more complex ones in just a few hours. As soon as they discovered the problem, they immediately contacted the PHP operations team. At almost the same time, Google's cybersecurity team and OpenAI's team also discovered this major vulnerability. After discovering the problem, the engineers had to race against time, working through the night to patch the vulnerability. They had to find a way to fix the hole before hackers discovered it, modifying nearly. 20 billion files and over 10,000 lines of code. They planned to release the PHP patch on October 22nd for all PHP-based websites to update their systems, but the secret leaked two days early. This is very serious, like finding a broken lock at home and calling a locksmith, only for the news to leak before they arrive; thieves would hear about it and rush to find a way in before the new lock is installed . The team feared bad actors would find.

the vulnerability and attack sites before the patch release, so they decided to move it up to Wednesday, October 21st, hoping to minimize the damage. So, with the patch now released , can we finally relax? Actually, no, because publishing a patch allows people to reverse-engineer the original vulnerability. Websites that haven't updated to the new PHP version yet could be attacked, and some hackers might study the patch to find new. vulnerabilities to exploit, making the patch release just another round of cat-and-mouse between hackers and engineers. When I first saw this news, I thought, "Good thing we have AI to help us find these vulnerabilities." Wrong! Experts say that, conversely, hackers can also use AI to find other vulnerabilities and launch attacks. As mentioned earlier, it’s not that no one discovered this PHP vulnerability before; it’s that people thought even. if it did exist, it was too complex to ……launch an attack. The security firm that discovered this PHP vulnerability noted that before AI, large-scale attacks like this were difficult to carry out manually, but with AI, that is no longer an obstacle. A cybersecurity researcher at the University of New South Wales in Australia pointed out that modern software is incredibly complex, and some vulnerabilities may go unnoticed for years. Discovering these vulnerabilities now doesn't mean new problems are appearing, but rather that our ability to detect them has changed.

In the past, catching errors in millions of lines of code was difficult even for a large team, but with AI, one person can do it and even launch more complex attacks; that is the biggest red flag this time. For example, a cyber risk firm based in Massachusetts in the U.S. found that with the help of AI, the number of digital flaws discovered recently has doubled compared to the same period last year. The widespread impact of this PHP vulnerability is highly significant, leading the cybersecurity community to. dub it "Black October." AI discovers cybersecurity flaws at such a rapid pace that it feels like a bottomless pit, leaving engineers scrambling to fix them; even FBI cybersecurity officials have stated that patching urban vulnerabilities has become an urgent task in the AI era. So, does AI actually enable hackers to launch large-scale attacks, or does it help engineers patch vulnerabilities faster? Expert opinions are currently divided. Some argue that the vulnerabilities AI finds are relatively rare or complex,. making them not necessarily easy to exploit, while others point out that an increase in discovered flaws doesn't equate to an increase in actual attacks . In fact, after the PHP vulnerability was exposed, there were thousands of attempted attacks in the 10 hours before the patch was released, and millions after; yet, to this day, no hackers have successfully broken through. Regarding this PHP incident, unless you host your own website,.

general internet users are not affected ; there is no need to download patches or update phone or computer software. Those who host their own sites should update to the latest PHP version immediately, and you will be fine. To prevent similar incidents, the usual advice applies: don't use the same password for every website. Otherwise, if an e-commerce platform is attacked and your password leaks, hackers can use those credentials to try and log into other sites. Next, for household electronics like phones, computers, or. internet-connected smart appliances, it's best to enable automatic software updates so you don't forget to patch them and give hackers an opening. Lastly, I want to ask you: do you think AI is a good thing? Or have we just invented another giant rock to drop on our own feet? Leave a comment and let me know. A quick reminder: next Tuesday at 8:00 PM, I will be hosting a livestream in the "International News Bootcamp" LINE community with Xiao Zhou from "Ren Zha Wen." If you haven't joined the bootcamp yet, join now; scan. this QR code to be taken directly to the bootcamp and see what we're working on. If you like this program, please share it with others. You can also subscribe to our official LINE account, which sends important news and this program to your phone daily; if you miss anything, all our reports are available on the LINE TODAY International channel. Global insights from Fanmei, curated international headlines for you every day, bringing you up to speed.

上個星期四，當台灣的大家在關心要不要放颱風假的時候，全球的網路軟體工程師都忙得要死、嚇到睡不著，因為全球高達7成以上網站使用的程式語言PHP，出現重大資安漏洞，如果不馬上修補，你的網站隨時都可能被駭客接管！因此很多網站都緊急下線進行搶修，導致一波網站離線潮。一個週末過去了，現在問題解決了嗎？4個字，戒慎恐懼，還不能掉以輕心。但整件事情最有趣的地方在於，這個漏洞其實是AI發現的。要不是AI，人類恐怕再過20年都不會發現。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解全球超過七成網站採用的 PHP 核心重大漏洞危機，以及這場被資安界稱為「黑色十月」事件的波及規模。
  • 揭秘人工智慧（AI）在資安攻防戰中的雙重角色，探討 AI 如何突破過去人力的限制，讓原本極難觸發的漏洞演變為真實威脅。
  • 掌握網站管理者與一般網路使用者在面對大規模零日攻擊時，應採取的具體自保建議與安全防護措施。

摘要

全球七成網站面臨的「黑色十月」危機

作者指出，全球超過 70% 網站使用的後端程式語言 PHP 爆出嚴重的核心安全漏洞。若未即時修補，駭客將能直接繞過網站介面並接管伺服器，使大量商業機密、個資暴露於危險之中。為了防堵損害擴大，美國國家安全局與荷蘭國家網路安全中心均建議停用相關對外網站，導致全球眾多政府機關、醫院、銀行及維基百科部分系統緊急離線；日本軟銀亦因緊急修補該漏洞，一度造成災害警報系統無法正常發布。

AI 介入挖掘：沉睡二十年的複雜漏洞重見天日

作者解釋，PHP 就如同網站幕後負責處理登入、搜尋與運算的工作人員，已存在超過三十年。過去該漏洞雖曾被發現，但因攻擊路徑極其複雜，資安界普遍認為難以利用。然而，加州資安公司與科技巨頭藉由 OpenAI 的先進語言模型，成功在極短時間內找到繞過限制並接管網站的方法。作者表示，這顯示在 AI 輔助下，過往需要龐大團隊在數百萬行程式碼中耗費數年才能尋得的微小瑕疵，如今單一人員即可迅速發掘並發動高複雜度的攻擊。

補丁外洩的搶修賽跑與 AI 帶來的資安兩難

在發現漏洞後，工程團隊日夜兼程修改了近百億個檔案與上萬行程式碼，原訂於 10 月 22 日釋出修補更新。不料情報提前兩天遭外洩，迫使官方將修復檔案提前至 10 月 21 日釋出以防範未然。作者強調，發布補丁並不代表危機結束，因為駭客也能透過逆向工程研究漏洞或尋找新破綻。雖然在補丁公開前後出現數以百萬計的攻擊嘗試，但所幸目前尚無成功的重大入侵案例，然而專家對 AI 是否讓攻擊端占據上風的疑慮依舊分歧。

大眾應對指引與數位防護之道

針對這場風暴，作者釐清指出，除非使用者自行架設並管理網站，否則一般網友無須為此下載特定補丁或更新手機電腦。作者提醒，自行架站者應立即更新至最新版本的 PHP；而一般大眾為了長遠的數位安全，應落實不重複使用同一組密碼的原則，並為手機、電腦與智慧聯網家電開啟自動軟體更新，以降低在其他連鎖攻擊中受害的風險。
